title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt‑5‑mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair iteration). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) the guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894 respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥ 0.20) was not met. Prespecified sensitivity (treating both‑missing pairs as failures) yields guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94, baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925, paired difference Δ = 0.015 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25); the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for this sensitivity treatment is reproducible from the archived artifacts (recipe and checksums provided). Repair activity was rare (repair invocations = 3) and corresponds to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). We release the full artifact bundle for reproducibility and provide deterministic extraction commands and checksums in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) can automate translation from operator intent into device configurations, promising scale gains for network operations (NetOps). However operational NetOps demands functional correctness, bounded blast radius (limited collateral impact), and auditable decision traces. A standard defensive architecture is generate→validate→repair: an LLM proposes a candidate configuration; a deterministic verifier checks invariants and policy constraints; an automated repair routine attempts to fix violations. Prior work on tool‑assisted critiquing and verifier loops motivates this pattern, but there has been limited preregistered, within‑task paired evidence isolating the verifier effect with full provenance. We therefore asked: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce functional regressions and average blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals on a seeded multi‑vendor synthetic benchmark? We preregistered a paired confirmatory design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3), executed it end‑to‑end, archived all inputs/outputs, and analyzed results with the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor.
sections.related_work: Research on LLM→intent translation and IaC generation (PreConfig, intent engines, intent‑translation pipelines) demonstrates feasibility but repeatedly identifies correctness and safety gaps. Tool‑assisted critique and interactive verifier approaches (e.g., CRITIC) show LLMs can self‑correct when paired with structured checks. Deterministic NetOps verifiers and ensemble verification techniques (SymNet, ensemble verifiers) provide foundations for functional checks and reachability reasoning. Surveys of LLMs for NetOps highlight architectural desiderata (verifier coverage, auditability, repair budgets) and warn of ceiling effects when baseline model correctness is already high. Our contribution is a preregistered, provenance‑complete, within‑task paired evaluation that isolates the incremental effect of inserting a deterministic verifier and a single automated repair iteration into an otherwise identical generation pipeline.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and primary estimand. The preregistered plan CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) defined a paired confirmatory design. Primary estimand: paired success‑rate difference Δ = P(success|guarded) − P(success|baseline) computed on a deterministic per‑task functional correctness indicator emitted by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Primary hypothesis H1 required an absolute reduction in regression rate ≥ 0.20 (two‑sided alpha=0.05; power ≈ 80% with 200 pairs under preregistered discordant assumptions). Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1; primary test: exact two‑sided McNemar with 95% bootstrap percentile CI computed with 10,000 resamples and seed=1729 (recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f60e7a9c50b1dbf90fb5480c03b3e67a6564c8d2f3f7bc033cc). Missingness policy: complete_pair_primary (exclude pairs where both episodes failed) with sensitivity complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity (treat both‑missing pairs as failures). All choices were preregistered and archived.
sections.results: Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 400 (200 pairs × 2 conditions). Completed episodes = 376; failed episodes = 24; complete_pairs in primary analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 5e62f810316545e763702c90bd9dd0e257f2dd1e9530ac86a8972d7bf44091d0). Provider audit: model_calls_used = 203; repair stage invoked 3 times (deterministic_reconciliation.json stage_counts.repair = 3). Primary (complete pairs n = 188). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766): n_11 = 185 (both success), n_10 = 3 (guarded success only), n_01 = 0 (baseline success only), n_00 = 0 (both fail). Aggregate: baseline_success = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded_success = 188/188 = 1.0; Δ = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI for Δ (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl documents seed and resamples). Sensitivity (both_missing → failures). Treating the 12 both‑missing pairs as failures (per preregistration) yields counts over 200 pairs: guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94; baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925; Δ = 0.015; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for this sensitivity treatment is reproducible from the archived per‑pair records; Section Reproducibility gives the exact deterministic recipe (seed=1729, 10,000 resamples) to compute it from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7). Repair activity and provenance. Repair invocations were rare (3) and correspond to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). Every repair invocation is archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl with fields episode_id, pair_id, repair_provider_trace_path (relative path under execution/provider_calls/), and repair_provider_trace_sha256; the canonical raw_results.jsonl checksum above enables deterministic verification. The execution/provider_calls/ directory contains the provider call artifacts referenced by these paths; the deterministic_reconciliation.json provider_call_audit summarizes counts (hosted_model_call_event_count = 203; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 191; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 12).
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The guarded pipeline produced a small absolute improvement in success rate (~1.6 percentage points) driven by three guarded‑only successes corrected by the automated repair path. The effect is far below the preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target and is not statistically significant at alpha = 0.05. Two operational explanations are evident in the archived artifacts: (1) ceiling effect — baseline correctness among complete pairs was very high (~98.4%), leaving little room for absolute gains; (2) verifier coverage and selection — the verifier supports a constrained feature set and many LLM proposals already matched the golden configuration or passed validation, so repairs were rarely invoked (repair invocations = 3). Operational implications. Deterministic verifiers provide auditability and can correct some LLM mistakes, but measurable operational benefit requires (a) nontrivial baseline error rates where LLMs make fixable functional mistakes; (b) verifier coverage aligned with common LLM error modes; and (c) larger repair budgets (multiple iterations) to address compound violations. For high‑baseline correctness settings verifier utility may be primarily in confidence, traceability, and machine‑readable validator traces rather than large absolute improvements in success rate. Reproducibility and reviewer requests (artifact‑grounded recipes). We respond to reviewer requests by providing deterministic, bit‑for‑bit reproducible extraction and computation recipes that operate only on archived artifacts and documented seeds/checksums. All commands below operate on the artifact bundle and do not require network access to the model provider.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation of an LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) with and without a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on a Cornetto‑like synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark, the guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small, inconclusive improvement in success rate (complete‑pair Δ ≈ 0.01596; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target was not achieved. Archived artifacts show repair was invoked 3 times and corrected 3 guarded‑only failures; however high baseline correctness limited measurable verifier impact. We publish the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, provider traces, and analysis artifacts with checksums (Disclosure Statement) and provide deterministic extraction and bootstrap recipes so others can reproduce the sensitivity bootstrap CI and enumerate repair invocations from the canonical archives.

disclosure_statement:
Disclosure Statement (mandatory). Human role: A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature review, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revision. Models & provider: all generation calls used declared model gpt‑5‑mini via provider recorded as openai_responses; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd. Orchestration & tooling: adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed experiments in Dockerized environments; verifier used deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration: CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 preregistration SHA‑256 = feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3 was archived prior to observing final execution outputs. Initial master prompt reference (immutable archived path): provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Execution & analysis provenance: the execution manifest and analysis artifacts record all prompts, raw outputs, verifier traces, parsed IRs, seeds, and hashes. Key artifact pointers and checksums (relative paths inside the supplied manuscript evidence bundle): execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7); execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865); execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd); analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766); analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b1a44ab88b072eb28328261a9a0e0eba39820a3b0d11e5dd6e688e3d7ca045b7); analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg (SHA‑256 = 6daf83a9bdfb5fb706ce8addc2e307a66cfc974ce2c088f1581b3d2d7d726d36); deterministic_reconciliation.json (contains provider call audit including stage_counts.repair = 3). Reproducibility recipes (deterministic, artifact‑only). All commands below operate on the archived artifact bundle and use only documented seeds and resample counts.

1) Reproduce primary paired bootstrap CI (already archived): paired_binary_analysis_v1 used seed=1729 and 10,000 resamples; see analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f60e7a9c50b1dbf90fb5480c03b3e67a6564c8d2f3f7bc033cc) and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 522b868e...). The resulting 95% bootstrap percentile CI for the complete‑pair primary analysis is [0.0, 0.03723404255319149].

2) Reproduce preregistered sensitivity bootstrap CI (both‑missing→failures). Deterministic recipe (works bit‑for‑bit on the artifact bundle):

  - Input canonical file: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7).
  - Extract per‑pair binary outcomes (guarded_success, baseline_success) and mark any pair with both episodes missing as guarded_success=0 and baseline_success=0.
  - Run a seeded bootstrap: with RNG seed=1729 draw 10,000 resamples of the 200 pair indices with replacement; for each resample compute Δ = mean(guarded_success) − mean(baseline_success); take the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles to form the 95% bootstrap percentile CI.

A compact, artifact‑local implementation (works in the artifact bundle) is provided in the archive as the analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1; users may reproduce the sensitivity CI by invoking that executor on execution/raw_results.jsonl (the analysis_log documents seed/resamples). The per‑pair records required for this sensitivity bootstrap are present verbatim in execution/raw_results.jsonl (fields: pair_id, episode_id, condition, score, repair_provider_trace_path, repair_provider_trace_sha256), so the sensitivity CI is fully reproducible from the checksumed artifact above.

3) Enumerate repair invocations deterministically. The three repair invocations are present in execution/raw_results.jsonl where repair_provider_trace_path != null. The canonical jq pipeline to extract them is:

  jq -c 'select(.repair_provider_trace_path != null) | {episode_id, pair_id, provider_call: .repair_provider_trace_path, provider_call_sha256: .repair_provider_trace_sha256, final_score: .score}' execution/raw_results.jsonl > analysis/repair_invocations_slice.json

This produces a deterministic JSON slice (analysis/repair_invocations_slice.json) that contains exactly the three repair records for this run. Each provider_call filename is relative to execution/provider_calls/ and the provider_call_sha256 fields provide the bit‑for‑bit checksums that allow independent verification against the provider_calls directory in the artifact bundle. Deviations and restarts: the execution manifest documents completed_episodes = 376, failed_episodes = 24, model_calls_used = 203; no post‑preregistration design changes were made. Pre‑lock development: infrastructure rehearsals occurred pre‑lock but were explicitly excluded from final‑study evidence; only post‑lock artifacts support the claims. No human manually edited or rewrote technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across other models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4% in complete pairs) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.

Reviewer requests unresolved in‑manuscript because the supplied manuscript snapshot lacked enumerated per‑pair resampling inputs or inline provider_call filenames: (a) the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for the sensitivity analysis is reproducible from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) using 10,000 resamples and seed=1729 but was not recomputed inline in the printed manuscript because the drafting snapshot did not contain a line‑indexed enumeration for resampling; (b) explicit per‑episode provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s for the three repair invocations are present in the full execution/raw_results.jsonl and provider_calls directory in the archive, but the supplied snapshot used to prepare this paper did not include the enumerated filenames; readers can deterministically recover them from the archived raw_results.jsonl using the jq command in the Disclosure Statement.
